# ADR: Approved role definitions reach the agent runtime as a compiled rendering

## 1. Context

An agent filling a named role in a process step is instantiated by
the harness from its load point, `.claude/agents/<name>.md`, whose
front-matter it reads as the subagent's contract and whose body it
reads as the role's prompt. What a role *is* stands elsewhere: the six
approved [role definitions](../basis/roles/) in `basis/roles/` —
lead-pm, lead-po, lead-solutions-architect, lead-product-designer,
cold-reviewer, researcher — each carrying, in its front-matter, the
runtime keys the harness honors (`name`, `description`, `tools`,
`maxTurns`) alongside the shop's identity keys it does not read
(`type`, `id`, `owner`, `status`, `approved`, `version`, `created`,
`updated`), and in its body a Document History and links written
relative to `basis/`. On 2026-09-03 no `.claude/agents/` existed on
this branch, and the two agents the harness offered — `lead-architect`
and `lead-po` — came from the frozen corpus through the `main`
checkout: 0 of 6 approved roles instantiable from an approved source
([init-roles-availability](../initiatives/init-roles-availability.md),
For whom; [sess-2026-09-03-a](../sessions/sess-2026-09-03-a.md),
evidence). The question the discovery conversation put to the
authority was in what form an approved definition stands at the load
point.

The pre-state held one exemplar of the answer for another definition
kind: the [skill-rendering](../basis/processes/skill-rendering.md)
process, approved 2026-09-02, renders approved process definitions to
`.claude/skills/` through `compile_process.py`, and a principles
rendering (`compile_principles.py` → `.claude/shop/principles.md`)
stood outside any process. Three working principles bear directly:
`single-source-of-truth` (every appearance of a definition other than
its home is a reference or a generated rendering), `governed-context`
(everything loaded into an agent's context traces to an approved
definition), and `least-context` (an activity loads the minimum
context necessary).

**The escalation that settled it.** The decision is the authority's,
so it records under `right: escalation`. The fork reached the
authority as the lead-pm's options in the discovery conversation for
init-roles-availability on 2026-09-03 (work item lead-wm8n5,
brainstorm form; recorded in sess-2026-09-03-a), and the authority
ruled in its words: "Render the role rather than use verbatim,
sibling process for now, more comprehensive work later." The ruling
entered the initiative's Document History (v1) and the solutions
architect role attached its feasibility verdict under it. This record
is authored after the ruling was applied — the
[role-rendering](../basis/processes/role-rendering.md) process
approved (v5) and run, six roles rendered by
[`compile_role.py`](../basis/tools/compile_role.py), the instantiation
of `lead-po` from the rendering demonstrated
([feat-roles-availability](../features/feat-roles-availability.md),
v6) — as the decision's record, the reasons having stood only in the
session record and the initiative's history row.

Options that were real:

- **Place the definition file verbatim at the load point.** Declined,
  for the reasons the authority had before it: the definition's body
  carries a Document History and `basis`-relative links that do not
  belong in an agent prompt — the history is context the role does
  not need, and the links resolve from `basis/roles/`, not from the
  load point — and its front-matter carries the shop's identity keys
  the harness does not read; and under `single-source-of-truth` the
  copy at the load point is a second appearance of the definition,
  hence a rendering either way — placing it verbatim only forgoes the
  strip and the link resolution while still owing the same currency
  check against the definition.
- **A two-layer render — a lean prompt plus the rest reachable from
  it.** Not chosen now: the ruling's "more comprehensive work later"
  carried it forward rather than rejecting it. The single-layer render
  met the initiative's measure within its one-session appetite — the
  architect's feasibility verdict read the render as a strip, a
  digest, and placement — so a second loadable form with no exemplar
  was not needed to deliver the outcome. This decision does not
  foreclose it (§4).
- **One generalized rendering process over skills and roles.** This
  option answers a different question — which process carries the
  rendering — and is the ruling's second clause, "sibling process for
  now". It is a separate decision: its options (one generalized
  process, or a sibling of skill-rendering) are not this record's
  options; its reasons (one exemplar of the pattern, so generalizing
  was premature; two near-identical processes may drift, which is why
  lead-sx9xj — fold the siblings, bring the principles rendering under
  a process — is its review trigger) are not this record's reasons;
  and its reversal — folding the siblings under lead-sx9xj — reverses
  it without touching what this record decides. Under the typedef's
  one-decision rule it is split out and named in this record's
  Document History as a candidate for its own run. This record takes
  as pre-state fact that the role-rendering process is the process
  maintaining the rendering, without deciding that process's shape.

Screened against the
[architecture principle set](../basis/architecture-principles.md):
conforms. `bidirectional-conformance` — the definition is the
authoritative design and the rendering conforms to it; the maintaining
process checks both directions, forward (an approved definition with
nothing at the load point is a `missing` finding) and reverse (a
rendering with no approved source is `stale` or `unrecognized`), and
the ruling was a recorded activity before it was applied (the
initiative's v1 row, the session record). `local-comprehension` — an
agent filling a role works at the inside-a-shop level, and the
rendering is performable from alone: its links resolve at the load
point and its history is stripped, so nothing below the level is read
to instantiate the role; the derivation from `least-context` is what
the strip serves. `knowable-shape` — the lead shop's description of
what stands at its load point is the role-rendering definition's Data
section, readable without opening the compiler, and every rendering
names its `source` and `source-digest`. `actor-neutral-discipline` —
the rendering, the check, and the reconciliation attach to the
role-rendering process and the solutions architect role, with the
same records whoever runs a step. `intent-provenance` — the ruling
traces to the originator's framing through the initiative's history.
`contracts-between-contexts` — no Bounded Context is touched, so
nothing crosses a contract. No principle is unsatisfied; nothing is
escalated.

## 2. Decision

An approved role definition reaches the agent runtime only as a
rendering — the agent file that `basis/tools/compile_role.py`
generates from the definition and places at the load point as
`.claude/agents/<name>.md` — never as the definition file placed
there as it stands.

## 3. Consequences

- The load point holds renderings, never definitions. What changes:
  `.claude/agents/<name>.md` is a generated file — the runtime keys
  plus `source` and `source-digest`, the definition's body without its
  Document History, every relative link resolved for the load point —
  and a hand edit there is overwritten at the next reconciliation. For
  whom: every agent filling a role, and the solutions architect role,
  which runs the compiler and reconciles. Cost: a second compiler to
  maintain beside `compile_process.py` (`compile_role.py`, experiment
  apparatus by its own header); forecloses: tuning a prompt at the
  load point — a change to what an agent operates from goes through
  the definition and its owner.
- Currency is owed after every definition change. What changes: an
  amended definition is not what the runtime instantiates until it is
  re-rendered; the interval is a `diverged` finding of the maintaining
  process. For whom: the owner amending a role, and the architect
  running the process. Cost: a run of role-rendering after each
  approval; until it runs, the runtime instantiates the previous
  rendering (lead-ghaiq records the same interval for skills).
- Approval gates instantiation at render time. What changes: the
  compiler renders only a definition with `status: approved`, so a
  draft role has no rendering and cannot be instantiated from the
  load point. For whom: role authors and the owner. Forecloses:
  exercising a draft role through the load point; a draft is exercised
  only once approved, or by a mechanism this decision does not
  provide.
- The runtime contract of a role definition is the compiler's
  key list. What changes: which front-matter keys pass through to the
  harness — `name`, `description`, `tools`, `maxTurns`, and the
  optional harness keys the compiler names — is decided in the
  compiler; a key the harness later honors reaches the runtime only
  when the compiler passes it. For whom: the role-definition typedef's
  owner and the solutions architect role. Cost: one compiler change
  per new key, and the role-rendering re-render that follows.
- No bound on Bounded Context shops. The decision covers the lead
  shop's own load point and its six roles: no Bounded Context exists
  on this branch (the initiative's Decomposition names none) and no
  contract carries the rule. Extending it — a BC shop's roles reach
  its runtime as renderings — would be a guardrail decision of the
  solutions architect role, not taken here.

## 4. Reversibility

Reversible at moderate cost. The definitions are untouched by the
decision — the rendering is a function of the definition and the
declared load point, nothing else — so reverting to verbatim placement
is: retire the compiler's render, amend the role-rendering process
(its `check` and `reconcile` steps assume the compiler), and re-place
six files; feat-roles-availability's scenarios speak of a role
"current with its approved definition" and hold under either form. A
move to a two-layer render is the smaller change: a second loadable
form in the compiler, the process's Data section amended. Review
triggers: lead-sx9xj — the comprehensive rendering work the authority
named, which reopens the loadable form alongside the process shape; a
harness that reads a role definition in the shop's own form, or stops
honoring the compiled form; a role whose prompt needs something the
single-layer rendering cannot carry.

Right: `escalation`, the fork the lead-pm put to the authority; §1 names it. Status draft pending the screen. |

    28	(`type`, `id`, `owner`, `status`, `approved`, `version`, `created`,

    30	relative to `basis/`. On 2026-09-03 no `.claude/agents/` existed on
    31	this branch, and the two agents the harness offered — `lead-architect`
    32	and `lead-po` — came from the frozen corpus through the `main`
    33	checkout: 0 of 6 approved roles instantiable from an approved source
    34	([init-roles-availability](../initiatives/init-roles-availability.md),
    35	For whom; [sess-2026-09-03-a](../sessions/sess-2026-09-03-a.md),
    36	evidence). The question the discovery conversation put to the
    37	authority was in what form an approved definition stands at the load
    38	point.
    39	
    40	The pre-state held one exemplar of the answer for another definition
    41	kind: the [skill-rendering](../basis/processes/skill-rendering.md)
    42	process, approved 2026-09-02, renders approved process definitions to
    43	`.claude/skills/` through `compile_process.py`, and a principles
    44	rendering (`compile_principles.py` → `.claude/shop/principles.md`)
    45	stood outside any process. Three working principles bear directly:
    46	`single-source-of-truth` (every appearance of a definition other than
    47	its home is a reference or a generated rendering), `governed-context`
    48	(everything loaded into an agent's context traces to an approved
    49	definition), and `least-context` (an activity loads the minimum
    50	context necessary).

    53	so it records under `right: escalation`. The fork reached the
    54	authority as the lead-pm's options in the discovery conversation for
    55	init-roles-availability on 2026-09-03 (work item lead-wm8n5,
    56	brainstorm form; recorded in sess-2026-09-03-a), and the authority
    57	ruled in its words: "Render the role rather than use verbatim,
    58	sibling process for now, more comprehensive work later." The ruling
    59	entered the initiative's Document History (v1) and the solutions
    60	architect role attached its feasibility verdict under it. This record
    61	is authored after the ruling was applied — the
    62	[role-rendering](../basis/processes/role-rendering.md) process
    63	approved (v5) and run, six roles rendered by
    64	[`compile_role.py`](../basis/tools/compile_role.py), the instantiation
    65	of `lead-po` from the rendering demonstrated
    66	([feat-roles-availability](../features/feat-roles-availability.md),
    67	v6) — as the decision's record, the reasons having stood only in the
    68	session record and the initiative's history row.
    69	
    70	Options that were real:
    71	
    72	- **Place the definition file verbatim at the load point.** Declined,
    73	  for the reasons the authority had before it: the definition's body
    74	  carries a Document History and `basis`-relative links that do not
    75	  belong in an agent prompt — the history is context the role does
    76	  not need, and the links resolve from `basis/roles/`, not from the
    77	  load point — and its front-matter carries the shop's identity keys
    78	  the harness does not read; and under `single-source-of-truth` the
    79	  copy at the load point is a second appearance of the definition,
    80	  hence a rendering either way — placing it verbatim only forgoes the
    81	  strip and the link resolution while still owing the same currency
    82	  check against the definition.
    83	- **A two-layer render — a lean prompt plus the rest reachable from
    84	  it.** Not chosen now: the ruling's "more comprehensive work later"
    85	  carried it forward rather than rejecting it. The single-layer render
    86	  met the initiative's measure within its one-session appetite — the
    87	  architect's feasibility verdict read the render as a strip, a
    88	  digest, and placement — so a second loadable form with no exemplar
    89	  was not needed to deliver the outcome. This decision does not
    90	  foreclose it (§4).
    91	- **One generalized rendering process over skills and roles.** This
    92	  option answers a different question — which process carries the
    93	  rendering — and is the ruling's second clause, "sibling process for
    94	  now". It is a separate decision: its options (one generalized
    95	  process, or a sibling of skill-rendering) are not this record's
    96	  options; its reasons (one exemplar of the pattern, so generalizing
    97	  was premature; two near-identical processes may drift, which is why
    98	  lead-sx9xj — fold the siblings, bring the principles rendering under
    99	  a process — is its review trigger) are not this record's reasons;
   100	  and its reversal — folding the siblings under lead-sx9xj — reverses
   101	  it without touching what this record decides. Under the typedef's
   102	  one-decision rule it is split out and named in this record's
   103	  Document History as a candidate for its own run. This record takes
   104	  as pre-state fact that the role-rendering process is the process
   105	  maintaining the rendering, without deciding that process's shape.
   106	
   107	Screened against the
   108	[architecture principle set](../basis/architecture-principles.md):
   109	conforms. `bidirectional-conformance` — the definition is the
   110	authoritative design and the rendering conforms to it; the maintaining
   111	process checks both directions, forward (an approved definition with
   112	nothing at the load point is a `missing` finding) and reverse (a
   113	rendering with no approved source is `stale` or `unrecognized`), and
   114	the ruling was a recorded activity before it was applied (the
   115	initiative's v1 row, the session record). `local-comprehension` — an
   116	agent filling a role works at the inside-a-shop level, and the
   117	rendering alone suffices for that work: its links resolve at the load
   118	point and its history is stripped, so nothing below the level is read
   119	to instantiate the role; the derivation from `least-context` is what
   120	the strip serves. `knowable-shape` — the lead shop's description of
   121	what stands at its load point is the role-rendering definition's Data
   122	section, readable without opening the compiler, and every rendering
   123	names its `source` and `source-digest`. `actor-neutral-discipline` —
   124	the rendering, the check, and the reconciliation attach to the
   125	role-rendering process and the solutions architect role, with the
   126	same records whoever runs a step. `intent-provenance` — the ruling
   127	traces to the originator's framing through the initiative's history.
   128	`contracts-between-contexts` — no Bounded Context is touched, so
   129	nothing crosses a contract. No principle is unsatisfied; nothing is
   130	escalated.
   131

   133	
   134	An approved role definition reaches the agent runtime only as a
   135	rendering — the agent file that `basis/tools/compile_role.py`
   136	generates from the definition and places at the load point as
   137	`.claude/agents/<name>.md` — never as the definition file placed
   138	there as it stands.
   139	
   140	## 3. Consequences
   141	
   142	- The load point holds renderings, never definitions. What changes:
   143	  `.claude/agents/<name>.md` is a generated file — the runtime keys
   144	  plus `source` and `source-digest`, the definition's body without its
   145	  Document History, every relative link resolved for the load point —
   146	  and a hand edit there is overwritten at the next reconciliation. For
   147	  whom: every agent filling a role, and the solutions architect role,
   148	  which runs the compiler and reconciles. Cost: a second compiler to
   149	  maintain beside `compile_process.py` (`compile_role.py`, experiment
   150	  apparatus by its own header); forecloses: tuning a prompt at the
   151	  load point — a change to what an agent operates from goes through
   152	  the definition and its owner.
   153	- Currency is owed after every definition change. What changes: an
   154	  amended definition is not what the runtime instantiates until it is
   155	  re-rendered; the interval is a `diverged` finding of the maintaining
   156	  process. For whom: the owner amending a role, and the architect
   157	  running the process. Cost: a run of role-rendering after each
   158	  approval; until it runs, the runtime instantiates the previous
   159	  rendering (lead-ghaiq records the same interval for skills).
   160	- Approval gates instantiation at render time. What changes: the
   161	  compiler renders only a definition with `status: approved`, so a
   162	  draft role has no rendering and cannot be instantiated from the
   163	  load point. For whom: role authors and the owner. Forecloses:
   164	  exercising a draft role through the load point; a draft is exercised
   165	  only once approved, or by a mechanism this decision does not
   166	  provide.
   167	- The runtime contract of a role definition is the compiler's
   168	  key list. What changes: which front-matter keys pass through to the
   169	  harness — `name`, `description`, `tools`, `maxTurns`, and the
   170	  optional harness keys the compiler names — is decided in the
   171	  compiler; a key the harness later honors reaches the runtime only
   172	  when the compiler passes it. For whom: the role-definition typedef's
   173	  owner and the solutions architect role. Cost: one compiler change
   174	  per new key, and the role-rendering re-render that follows.
   175	- No bound on Bounded Context shops. The decision covers the lead
   176	  shop's own load point and its six roles: no Bounded Context exists
   177	  on this branch (the initiative's Decomposition names none) and no
   178	  contract carries the rule. Extending it — a BC shop's roles reach
   179	  its runtime as renderings — would be a guardrail decision of the
   180	  solutions architect role, not taken here.
   181	
   182	## 4. Reversibility
   183	
   184	Reversible at moderate cost. The definitions are untouched by the
   185	decision — the rendering is a function of the definition and the
   186	declared load point, nothing else — so reverting to verbatim placement
   187	is: retire the compiler's render, amend the role-rendering process
   188	(its `check` and `reconcile` steps assume the compiler), and re-place
   189	six files; feat-roles-availability's scenarios speak of a role
   190	"current with its approved definition" and hold under either form. A
   191	move to a two-layer render is the smaller change: a second loadable
   192	form in the compiler, the process's Data section amended. Review
   193	triggers: lead-sx9xj — the comprehensive rendering work the authority
   194	named, which reopens the loadable form alongside the process shape; a
   195	harness that reads a role definition in the shop's own form, or stops
   196	honoring the compiled form; a role whose prompt needs something the
   197	single-layer rendering cannot carry.
   198

   200	
   201	| Version | Date | Kind | Entry |
   202	|---|---|---|---|
   203	| 1 | 2026-09-04 | update | Authored through the adr-authoring process for the authority's ruling of 2026-09-03 in the discovery conversation for init-roles-availability (lead-wm8n5), after the ruling was applied — role-rendering approved and run, 6 of 6 rendered and demonstrated — so the reasons, until now held only in the session record and the initiative's history row, stand in a decision record. Right: `escalation`, the fork the lead-pm put to the authority; §1 names it. The ruling's second clause — "sibling process for now" — is split out under the one-decision rule as a candidate for its own run: *the rendering of roles is carried by a sibling process of skill-rendering rather than by one generalized rendering process* (review trigger lead-sx9xj). `.claude/agents/<name>.md`, whose front-matter it reads as the
subagent's contract and whose body it reads as the role's prompt.
What a role *is* stands elsewhere: the six approved
[role definitions](../basis/roles/) in `basis/roles/` — lead-pm,
lead-po, lead-solutions-architect, lead-product-designer,
cold-reviewer, researcher — each carrying, in its front-matter, the
runtime keys the harness honors (`name`, `description`, `tools`,
`maxTurns`) alongside the shop's identity keys it does not read
(`type`, `id`, `owner`, `status`, `approved`, `version`, `created`,
`updated`), and in its body a Document History and links written
relative to `basis/`. On 2026-09-03 no `.claude/agents/` existed on
this branch, and the two agents the harness offered — `lead-architect`
and `lead-po` — came from the frozen corpus through the `main`
checkout: 0 of 6 approved roles instantiable from an approved source
([init-roles-availability](../initiatives/init-roles-availability.md),
For whom; [sess-2026-09-03-a](../sessions/sess-2026-09-03-a.md),
evidence). The question the discovery conversation put to the
authority was in what form an approved definition stands at the load
point.

The pre-state held one exemplar of the answer for another definition
kind: the [skill-rendering](../basis/processes/skill-rendering.md)
process, approved 2026-09-02, renders approved process definitions to
`.claude/skills/` through `compile_process.py`, and a principles
rendering (`compile_principles.py` → `.claude/shop/principles.md`)
stood outside any process. Three working principles bear directly:
`single-source-of-truth` (every appearance of a definition other than
its home is a reference or a generated rendering), `governed-context`
(everything loaded into an agent's context traces to an approved
definition), and `least-context` (an activity loads the minimum
context necessary).

**The escalation that settled it.** The decision is the authority's,
so it records under `right: escalation`. The fork reached the
authority as the lead-pm's options in the discovery conversation for
init-roles-availability on 2026-09-03 (work item lead-wm8n5 — the
discovery conversation, brainstorm form; recorded in
sess-2026-09-03-a), and the authority ruled in its words: "Render the
role rather than use verbatim, sibling process for now, more
comprehensive work later." The ruling entered the initiative's
Document History (v1) and the solutions architect role attached its
feasibility verdict under it. This record is authored retroactively:
its `date` is the decision date, 2026-09-03, and its `created` the
record's authoring date, 2026-09-04 — after the ruling was applied,
the [role-rendering](../basis/processes/role-rendering.md) process
approved (v5) and run, six roles rendered by
[`compile_role.py`](../basis/tools/compile_role.py), the instantiation
of `lead-po` from the rendering demonstrated
([feat-roles-availability](../features/feat-roles-availability.md),
v6) — as the decision's record, the reasons having stood only in the
session record and the initiative's history row.

Options that were real:

- **Place the definition file verbatim at the load point.** Declined,
  for the reasons the authority had before it: the definition's body
  carries a Document History and `basis`-relative links that do not
  belong in an agent prompt — the history is context the role does
  not need, and the links resolve from `basis/roles/`, not from the
  load point — and its front-matter carries the shop's identity keys
  the harness does not read; and under `single-source-of-truth` the
  copy at the load point is a second appearance of the definition,
  hence a rendering either way — placing it verbatim only forgoes the
  strip and the link resolution while still owing the same currency
  check against the definition.
- **A two-layer render — a lean prompt plus the rest reachable from
  it.** Not chosen now: the ruling's "more comprehensive work later"
  carried it forward rather than rejecting it. The single-layer render
  met the initiative's measure within its one-session appetite — the
  architect's feasibility verdict read the render as a strip, a
  digest, and placement — so a second loadable form with no exemplar
  was not needed to deliver the outcome. This decision does not
  foreclose it (§4).
- **One generalized rendering process over skills and roles.** This
  option answers a different question — which process carries the
  rendering — and is the ruling's second clause, "sibling process for
  now": a separate decision with its own options, reasons, and
  reversal, split out under the typedef's one-decision rule as a
  candidate named in this record's Document History. This record
  takes as pre-state fact that a maintaining rendering process exists
  — today, role-rendering — without deciding that process's shape.

Screened against the
[architecture principle set](../basis/architecture-principles.md):
conforms. `bidirectional-conformance` — the definition is the
authoritative design and the rendering conforms to it; the maintaining
process checks both directions, forward and reverse, through the
finding kinds role-rendering's O4 names — `missing` (an approved
definition with nothing at the load point), `diverged` (a rendering
not byte-equal to a fresh render), `stale` (a rendering whose source
does not stand approved), `unrecognized` (a load-point file that is no
rendering of any definition) — and the ruling was a recorded activity
before it was applied (the initiative's v1 row, the session record).
`local-comprehension` — an agent filling a role works at the
inside-a-shop level, and the rendering alone suffices for that work:
its links resolve at the load point and its history is stripped, so
nothing below the level is read to instantiate the role; the
derivation from `least-context` is what the strip serves.
`knowable-shape` — the lead shop's description of what stands at its
load point is the role-rendering definition's Data section, readable
without opening the compiler, and every rendering names its `source`
and `source-digest`. `actor-neutral-discipline` — the rendering, the
check, and the reconciliation attach to the role-rendering process and
the solutions architect role, with the same records whoever runs a
step. `intent-provenance` — the intent entered through the lead shop's
operational contract, as the initiative's Framing records, the
discovery conversation being the process under that contract, and the
ruling traces to the originator's words through the initiative's
history. `contracts-between-contexts` — no Bounded Context is touched,
so nothing crosses a contract. No principle is unsatisfied; nothing is
escalated.

## 2. Decision

An approved role definition reaches the agent runtime only as a
rendering — the agent file the maintaining rendering process generates
from the definition and places at the load point as
`.claude/agents/<name>.md` — never as the definition file placed
there as it stands.

## 3. Consequences

- The load point holds renderings, never definitions. What changes:
  `.claude/agents/<name>.md` is a generated file — the runtime keys
  plus `source` and `source-digest`, the definition's body without its
  Document History, every relative link resolved for the load point —
  and a hand edit there is overwritten at the next reconciliation. For
  whom: every agent filling a role, and the solutions architect role,
  which runs the compiler and reconciles. Cost: a second compiler to
  maintain beside `compile_process.py` — today
  `basis/tools/compile_role.py`, the current instrument, held at
  experiment status: promotion out of that status is the owner's,
  through the annotations block the process-definition typedef carries
  (role-rendering's `promotion: experiment-local`), and nothing in
  this decision depends on the status. Forecloses: tuning a prompt at
  the load point — a change to what an agent operates from goes
  through the definition and its owner.
- Currency is owed after every definition change. What changes: an
  amended definition is not what the runtime instantiates until it is
  re-rendered; the interval is a `diverged` finding of the maintaining
  process. For whom: the owner amending a role, and the architect
  running the process. Cost: a run of role-rendering after each
  approval; until it runs, the runtime instantiates the previous
  rendering (lead-ghaiq — the run-record divergence, a run-record row
  written into a process definition diverging its carrier until the
  next run — records the same interval for skills).
- Approval gates instantiation at render time. What changes: the
  compiler renders only a definition with `status: approved`, so a
  draft role has no rendering and cannot be instantiated from the
  load point. For whom: role authors and the owner. Forecloses:
  exercising a draft role through the load point; a draft is exercised
  only once approved, or by a mechanism this decision does not
  provide.
- The runtime contract of a role definition is fixed in the design,
  and the compiler conforms to it. What changes: which front-matter
  keys pass through to the harness is decided by the
  [role-definition typedef](../basis/artifacts/role-definition.md)'s
  Required frontmatter — `name`, `description`, `tools`, `maxTurns`,
  its functional contract keys — plus the optional harness keys the
  role-rendering definition's Data section names; the compiler passes
  those and no others. A key the harness later honors reaches the
  runtime only once the typedef or the process definition admits it.
  For whom: the role-definition typedef's owner and the solutions
  architect role. Cost: a definition change per new key, the compiler
  change that conforms to it, and the role-rendering re-render that
  follows.
- No bound on Bounded Context shops. The decision covers the lead
  shop's own load point and its six roles: no Bounded Context exists
  on this branch (the initiative's Decomposition names none) and no
  contract carries the rule. Extending it — a BC shop's roles reach
  its runtime as renderings — would be a guardrail decision of the
  solutions architect role, not taken here.

## 4. Reversibility

Reversible at moderate cost. The definitions are untouched by the
decision — the rendering is a function of the definition and the
declared load point, nothing else — so reverting to verbatim placement
is: retire the render, amend the role-rendering process (its `check`
and `reconcile` steps assume a compiler), and re-place six files;
feat-roles-availability's scenarios speak of a role "current with its
approved definition" and hold under either form. A move to a two-layer
render is the smaller change: a second loadable form in the compiler,
the process's Data section amended. Review triggers: lead-sx9xj — the
comprehensive rendering work the authority named (fold the sibling
processes, bring the principles rendering under a process), which
reopens the loadable form alongside the process shape; a harness that
reads a role definition in the shop's own form, or stops honoring the
compiled form; a role whose prompt needs something the single-layer
rendering cannot carry.

conforms. `bidirectional-conformance` — the definition is the
authoritative design and the rendering conforms to it; the maintaining
process checks both directions, forward and reverse, through the
finding kinds named in role-rendering's fourth outcome, O4 —
`missing` (an approved definition with nothing at the load point),

and `source-digest`. `actor-neutral-discipline` — the rendering, the

the solutions architect role, with the same records whoever runs a

ruling traces to the originator's words through the initiative's

so nothing crosses a contract. No principle is unsatisfied; nothing is

## 2. Decision

An approved role definition reaches the agent runtime only as a
rendering — the agent file the maintaining rendering process generates
from the definition and places at the load point as
`.claude/agents/<name>.md` — never as the definition file placed
there as it stands.

## 3. Consequences

- The load point holds renderings, never definitions. What changes:
  `.claude/agents/<name>.md` is a generated file — the runtime keys
  plus `source` and `source-digest`, the definition's body without its
  Document History, every relative link resolved for the load point —
  and a hand edit there is overwritten at the next reconciliation. For
  whom: every agent filling a role, and the solutions architect role,
  which runs the compiler and reconciles. Cost: a second compiler to
  maintain beside `compile_process.py` — today
  `basis/tools/compile_role.py`, the current instrument; the decision
  is tool-neutral, so the compiler's experiment status does not alter
  the cost. Forecloses: tuning a prompt at the load point — a change
  to what an agent operates from goes through the definition and its
  owner.
- Currency is owed after every definition change. What changes: an
  amended definition is not what the runtime instantiates until it is
  re-rendered; the interval is a `diverged` finding of the maintaining
  process. For whom: the owner amending a role, and the architect
  running the process. Cost: a run of role-rendering after each
  approval; until it runs, the runtime instantiates the previous
  rendering (lead-ghaiq — the run-record divergence, a run-record row
  written into a process definition diverging its carrier until the
  next run — records the same interval for skills).
- Approval gates instantiation at render time. What changes: the
  compiler renders only a definition with `status: approved`, so a
  draft role has no rendering and cannot be instantiated from the
  load point. For whom: role authors and the owner. Forecloses:
  exercising a draft role through the load point; a draft is exercised
  only once approved, or by a mechanism this decision does not
  provide.
- The runtime contract of a role definition is fixed in the design,
  and the compiler conforms to it. What changes: which front-matter
  keys pass through to the harness is decided by the
  [role-definition typedef](../basis/artifacts/role-definition.md)'s
  Required frontmatter — `name`, `description`, `tools`, `maxTurns`,
  its functional contract keys — plus the optional harness keys the
  role-rendering definition's Data section names; the compiler passes
  those and no others. A key the harness later honors reaches the
  runtime only once the typedef or the process definition admits it.
  For whom: the role-definition typedef's owner and the solutions
  architect role. Cost: a definition change per new key, the compiler
  change that conforms to it, and the role-rendering re-render that
  follows.
- No bound on Bounded Context shops. The decision covers the lead
  shop's own load point and its six roles: no Bounded Context exists
  on this branch (the initiative's Decomposition names none) and no
  contract carries the rule. Extending it — a BC shop's roles reach
  its runtime as renderings — would be a guardrail decision (a
  platform-guardrail decision, the architect role's domain), not
  taken here.

## 4. Reversibility

Reversible at moderate cost, design first. Reverting to verbatim
placement is: amend the role-rendering definition — the recorded
design change, whose Data section defines the loadable form and whose
`check` and `reconcile` steps assume a compiler; then run that
definition's `check` step, the reverse conformance check, which names
every rendering at the load point the amended design no longer calls
for, and retire them at reconciliation; then re-place the six
definitions. The definitions themselves are untouched by the decision
— the rendering is a function of the definition and the declared load
point, nothing else — and feat-roles-availability's scenarios speak
of a role "current with its approved definition", holding under
either form. A move to a two-layer render is the smaller change: the
process's Data section amended, a second loadable form in the
compiler. Review triggers: lead-sx9xj — the comprehensive rendering
work the authority named (fold the sibling processes, bring the
principles rendering under a process), which reopens the loadable
form alongside the process shape; a harness that reads a role
definition in the shop's own form, or stops honoring the compiled
form; a role whose prompt needs something the single-layer rendering
cannot carry.

# ADR: Approved role definitions reach the agent runtime as a compiled rendering

## 1. Context

An agent filling a named role in a process step is instantiated by
the harness — the agent runtime — from its load point,
`.claude/agents/<name>.md`, whose front-matter it reads as the
subagent's contract and whose body it reads as the role's prompt.
What a role *is* stands elsewhere: the six approved
[role definitions](../basis/roles/) in `basis/roles/`, each carrying,
in its front-matter, the runtime keys the harness honors (`name`,
`description`, `tools`, `maxTurns`) alongside the shop's identity
keys it does not read, and in its body a Document History and links
written relative to `basis/`. On 2026-09-03 no `.claude/agents/`
existed on this branch, and the two agents the harness offered —
`lead-architect` and `lead-po` — came from the frozen corpus: the
harness reads project-level agents from the repository's `main`
checkout, which this branch's worktree shares, so `main`'s
`.claude/agents/` reached sessions opened here. 0 of 6 approved roles
were instantiable from an approved source
([init-roles-availability](../initiatives/init-roles-availability.md),
For whom; [sess-2026-09-03-a](../sessions/sess-2026-09-03-a.md),
evidence). The question the discovery conversation put to the
authority was in what form an approved definition stands at the load
point.

The pre-state held one exemplar of the answer for another definition
kind: the [skill-rendering](../basis/processes/skill-rendering.md)
process, approved 2026-09-02, renders approved process definitions to
`.claude/skills/` through `compile_process.py`. Three working
principles bear directly: `single-source-of-truth` — every appearance
of a definition other than its home is a reference or a generated
rendering — `governed-context`, and `least-context`.

**The escalation that settled it.** The decision is the authority's,
so it records under `right: escalation`. The fork reached the
authority as the lead-pm's options in the discovery conversation for
init-roles-availability on 2026-09-03 (lead-wm8n5 — the discovery
conversation, brainstorm form; recorded in sess-2026-09-03-a), and
the authority ruled in its words: "Render the role rather than use
verbatim, sibling process for now, more comprehensive work later."
The ruling entered the initiative's Document History (v1). This
record is authored retroactively: its `date` is the decision date,
2026-09-03, and its `created` the record's authoring date, 2026-09-04
— after the ruling was applied, the
[role-rendering](../basis/processes/role-rendering.md) process
approved (v5) and run, six roles rendered by
[`compile_role.py`](../basis/tools/compile_role.py), the instantiation
of `lead-po` from the rendering demonstrated
([feat-roles-availability](../features/feat-roles-availability.md),
v6).

Options that were real:

- **Place the definition file verbatim at the load point.** Declined,
  for the reasons the authority had before it: the definition's body
  carries a Document History and `basis`-relative links that do not
  belong in an agent prompt — the history is context the role does
  not need, and the links resolve from `basis/roles/`, not from the
  load point — and its front-matter carries the shop's identity keys
  the harness does not read; and under `single-source-of-truth` even
  a verbatim copy would have to be generated and reconciled, so the
  real choice was what the generated form carries.
- **A two-layer render — a lean prompt plus the rest reachable from
  it.** Not chosen now: the ruling's "more comprehensive work later"
  carried it forward rather than rejecting it. The single-layer render
  — a strip, a digest, and placement, per the architect's feasibility
  verdict in the initiative's
  [Feasibility and usability](../initiatives/init-roles-availability.md#feasibility-and-usability)
  section — met the initiative's measure within its one-session
  appetite; a second loadable form with no exemplar was not needed.
  This decision does not foreclose it (§4).
- **One generalized rendering process over skills and roles.** This
  option answers a different question — which process carries the
  rendering — and is the ruling's second clause, "sibling process for
  now": a separate decision, split out under the typedef's
  one-decision rule. Candidate record: *the rendering of roles is
  carried by a sibling process of skill-rendering rather than one
  generalized rendering process*, carried in lead-sx9xj. This record
  takes as pre-state fact that a maintaining rendering process exists
  — today, role-rendering — without deciding that process's shape.

Screened against the
[architecture principle set](../basis/architecture-principles.md):
conforms.

- `bidirectional-conformance` — the definition is the authoritative
  design and the rendering conforms to it; the maintaining process
  checks both directions, forward and reverse, through the finding
  kinds named in role-rendering's fourth outcome, O4 — `missing` (an
  approved definition with nothing at the load point), `diverged` (a
  rendering not byte-equal to a fresh render), `stale` (a rendering
  whose source does not stand approved), `unrecognized` (a load-point
  file that is no rendering of any definition). The role-rendering
  definition (v5) was the design element the code conformed to; the
  decision itself stood recorded only in the initiative's history row
  and the session record from 2026-09-03 to 2026-09-04 — a recording
  gap this record closes.
- `local-comprehension` — an agent filling a role works at the
  inside-a-shop level, and the rendering alone suffices for that work:
  its links resolve at the load point and its history is stripped, so
  nothing beyond the rendering is read to instantiate the role; the
  derivation from `least-context` is what the strip serves.
- `knowable-shape` — the lead shop's description of what stands at
  its load point is the role-rendering definition's Data section, and
  every rendering names its `source` and `source-digest`.
- `actor-neutral-discipline` — the rendering, the check, and the
  reconciliation attach to the role-rendering process and the
  solutions architect role, with the same records whoever runs a step.
- `intent-provenance` — the intent entered through the lead shop's
  operational contract as the initiative's Framing records, the
  discovery conversation being the process under that contract, and
  the ruling traces to the originator's words through the initiative's
  history; that contract has no artifact on this branch — a shop-wide
  gap carried by lead-4kymc, not an exception of this decision.
- `contracts-between-contexts` — no Bounded Context is touched, so
  nothing crosses a contract.

No principle is unsatisfied; nothing is escalated.

## 2. Decision

An approved role definition reaches the agent runtime only as a
rendering — the agent file the maintaining rendering process generates
from the definition and places at the load point as
`.claude/agents/<name>.md` — never as the definition file placed
there as it stands.

## 3. Consequences

- The load point holds renderings, never definitions. What changes:
  `.claude/agents/<name>.md` is a generated file — the runtime keys
  plus `source` and `source-digest`, the definition's body without its
  Document History, every relative link resolved for the load point —
  and a hand edit there is overwritten at the next reconciliation. For
  whom: every agent filling a role, and the solutions architect role,
  which runs the compiler and reconciles. Cost: a second compiler to
  maintain beside `compile_process.py` — today
  `basis/tools/compile_role.py`, the current instrument; the decision
  is tool-neutral, so the compiler's experiment status does not alter
  the cost. Forecloses: tuning a prompt at the load point — a change
  to what an agent operates from goes through the definition and its
  owner.
- Currency is owed after every definition change. What changes: an
  amended definition is not what the runtime instantiates until it is
  re-rendered; the interval is a `diverged` finding of the maintaining
  process. For whom: the owner amending a role, and the architect
  running the process. Cost: a run of role-rendering after each
  approval; until it runs, the runtime instantiates the previous
  rendering (lead-ghaiq — the run-record divergence — records the same
  interval for skills).
- Approval gates instantiation at render time. What changes: the
  compiler renders only a definition with `status: approved`, so a
  draft role has no rendering and cannot be instantiated from the
  load point. For whom: role authors and the owner. Forecloses:
  exercising a draft role through the load point before approval.
- The runtime contract of a role definition is fixed in the design,
  and the compiler conforms to it. What changes: the front-matter keys
  that pass to the harness are those the
  [role-definition typedef](../basis/artifacts/role-definition.md)'s
  Required frontmatter names — `name`, `description`, `tools`,
  `maxTurns`, its functional contract keys — plus the optional harness
  keys the role-rendering definition's Data section names; the
  compiler passes those and no others, and a key the harness later
  honors reaches the runtime only once a definition admits it. For
  whom: the role-definition typedef's owner and the solutions
  architect role. Cost: a definition change per new key, the
  conforming compiler change, and the re-render.
- No bound on Bounded Context shops. The decision covers the lead
  shop's own load point and its six roles: no Bounded Context exists
  on this branch (the initiative's Decomposition names none) and no
  contract carries the rule. Extending it — a BC shop's roles reach
  its runtime as renderings — would be a guardrail decision — a
  decision on the platform guardrails Bounded Context shops build
  within, the architect role's domain — not taken here.

## 4. Reversibility

Reversible at moderate cost, design first. Reverting to verbatim
placement is: amend the role-rendering definition — the recorded
design change, whose Data section defines the loadable form and whose
`check` and `reconcile` steps assume a compiler; then run that
definition's `check` step — both directions — whose reverse findings
(`stale`, `unrecognized`) name every rendering the amended design no
longer calls for, retired at reconciliation; then re-place the six
definitions. The definitions themselves are untouched, and
feat-roles-availability's scenarios ("current with its approved
definition") hold under either form. A two-layer render is the
smaller change: the Data section amended, a second loadable form in
the compiler. Review triggers: lead-sx9xj — the comprehensive
rendering work the authority named (fold the sibling processes, bring
the principles rendering under a process), which reopens the loadable
form alongside the process shape; a harness that reads a role
definition in the shop's own form, or stops honoring the compiled
form; a role whose prompt needs something the single-layer rendering
cannot carry.
